claude_take: What strikes me across today's stories is how many institutions are being asked, or are asking themselves, whether they can still be trusted to self-govern. OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind's newly disclosed safety coordination and OpenAI's own decision to delay its IPO both signal caution, but they land the same week Gallup clocks a record 27% of US workers fearing technology will make their job obsolete outright -- the labs' reassurances and the public's anxiety are moving in opposite directions, not converging. Screen workers aren't waiting to find out if streamers will do better on their own: 750,000 of them are asking governments to just mandate local investment by law. And the Kennedy Center shows what happens when self-governance fails for reasons that have nothing to do with competence -- a fight over whose name goes on the building, not the institution's actual mission, is what shut its doors this week.
claude_take_title: A Fight Over a Name, Not a Mission

items.headline: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind Say They Have Quietly Coordinated on AI Safety for Weeks
items.summary: OpenAI's global policy chief Chris Lehane confirmed that OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind have been coordinating on AI safety measures for several weeks, following Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's weekend essay urging the industry to voluntarily slow the pace of frontier AI development. Lehane said the three labs don't believe a formal antitrust waiver is needed to collaborate on safety, adding that it is better to work together to prioritize it. The disclosure marks a rare moment of public coordination among the industry's fiercest competitors, coming just a day after President Trump publicly dismissed Amodei's slowdown call as unnecessary.

items.headline: Sam Altman Confirms OpenAI Is Delaying Its IPO to 2027, Citing AI Safety Concerns Over Market Conditions
items.summary: Sam Altman told Fortune that OpenAI has pushed its IPO timeline back to 2027, saying a public listing in 2026 would be ill-advised given the current moment for AI safety and alignment rather than any weakness in market appetite. Altman said the company feels no financial pressure to go public and will do so only once its readiness matches what the moment is like in society with the technology. The delay puts OpenAI a year or more behind rival Anthropic, which is targeting a listing before the end of 2026 at a valuation that could reach $2.3 trillion.

items.headline: 750,000-Strong Global Screen Coalition Urges Governments to Force Streamers to Fund Local Production
items.summary: A coalition of 23 screen industry organizations representing more than 750,000 workers across Canada, Australia and 13 European countries issued a joint statement at the Toronto International Film Festival calling on governments to require streaming platforms to invest directly in local film and television production. Signatories, including Canada's CMPA and Screen Producers Australia, warned that outdated content rules leave homegrown stories and independent producers increasingly exposed as streamers capture a growing share of viewing without matching local investment obligations. The statement adds fresh industry pressure just as several governments, including Canada's, weigh new streamer-contribution requirements.

items.headline: Canada Modernizes Decades-Old Film Co-Production Treaties With Spain and the UK at TIFF
items.summary: On the sidelines of the Toronto International Film Festival, Canada signed updated audiovisual co-production treaties with Spain and the United Kingdom, replacing an agreement with Spain that dated back to 1985. The new treaties widen the definition of a co-production to cover film, television and video works of any length or genre, letting qualifying projects count as a domestic production in both countries and access the corresponding public funding and incentives. Canadian Heritage Minister Marc Miller signed the deals alongside counterparts from Spain and the UK, aiming to make cross-border financing and production easier in a difficult financing environment for the industry.

items.headline: Gallup: Record 27% of US Workers Now Fear Technology Will Make Their Job Obsolete
items.summary: A new Gallup poll finds that 27% of US workers worry technology could soon make their job obsolete, a new high that is up seven points from a year ago and roughly double the 13% recorded when Gallup first asked the question in 2017. The fear is sharpest among younger workers, with 34% of those aged 18 to 44 citing it as their top job concern, surpassing more traditional worries like layoffs or wage cuts. The results, based on interviews conducted in August 2026, point to a rapid, broad-based shift in how Americans view AI-driven automation as an immediate threat to their livelihoods rather than a distant abstraction.

items.headline: Kennedy Center Board Votes to Close the Venue Hours After a Judge Blocks Trump's Name From the Building
items.summary: The Trump-aligned board of the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts voted to close most of the venue, citing what it called certain fiscal collapse, just hours after a federal judge ruled for a second time that Trump's name cannot be added to the building without congressional approval. The closure vote followed a tense board meeting in which Trump reportedly called in and berated a Democratic member of the panel. Trump has since suggested that planned renovations to the center, one of the nation's premier performing arts institutions, may not proceed at all unless the naming dispute is resolved in his favor, with an appeal to the Supreme Court expected.

items.headline: CFDA President Steven Kolb Takes Leave After Restraining a PETA Protester at New York Fashion Week
items.summary: Steven Kolb, president and CEO of the Council of Fashion Designers of America, is taking a leave of absence after video showed him grabbing and restraining a PETA activist who had stormed the runway during Cos's Spring 2027 show at New York Fashion Week. The protesters were demonstrating against the brand's use of wool, and Kolb, who leads American fashion's top trade body, later apologized and called his reaction completely out of character. The CFDA said it is conducting a full review, and the incident has become a flashpoint just as the fashion industry faces intensifying activist pressure over animal-derived materials during the fall show season.

items.headline: Zhuangzi's Butterfly Dream
items.headline_fr: Le rêve du papillon de Zhuangzi
items.summary: In an ancient parable, the Daoist philosopher Zhuangzi dreamed he was a butterfly, fluttering about with no awareness of being Zhuangzi, and upon waking could not tell whether he was a man who had dreamed he was a butterfly, or a butterfly now dreaming he was a man. The story is not really about dreaming at all; it challenges the assumption that waking experience gives us secure, fixed access to who and what we really are. Zhuangzi's broader Daoist philosophy treats rigid distinctions, self versus other, right versus wrong, human versus nature, as products of a limited perspective rather than the true shape of reality. The image endures because it captures something people still recognize: identity and certainty are far less stable than they feel from the inside.
items.summary_fr: Dans une parabole ancienne, le philosophe taoïste Zhuangzi rêva qu'il était un papillon, voletant sans la moindre conscience d'être Zhuangzi, et à son réveil, il ne put dire s'il était un homme ayant rêvé qu'il était un papillon, ou un papillon rêvant désormais qu'il était un homme. Ce récit ne parle pas vraiment de rêve : il remet en cause l'idée que l'expérience éveillée nous donnerait un accès sûr et stable à ce que nous sommes réellement. Dans sa philosophie taoïste plus large, Zhuangzi considère les distinctions rigides, entre soi et autrui, le vrai et le faux, l'humain et la nature, comme les produits d'un point de vue limité plutôt que la forme véritable de la réalité. Cette image perdure parce qu'elle touche à quelque chose que chacun reconnaît encore aujourd'hui : l'identité et la certitude sont bien moins stables qu'elles ne le paraissent de l'intérieur.
